gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ your passport at the check-in desk.
gaps.explanation: 'Lose' is the verb; 'loose' means not tight.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

gaps.hint: the standard verb with television and sport
gaps.explanation: 'Watch television' is the fixed collocation; 'look' needs 'at', and 'see television' is not used.

gaps.sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
gaps.hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
gaps.explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.

gaps.sentence: The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.
